=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1560-1566 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The `normalize_validation_signature` docstring (line 1563 in one report) says every hex run of 7-64 characters becomes `<sha>`, but `_VALIDATION_HEX_RUN_RE` now masks only full 40/64-hex SHAs or shorter runs that contain a digit.
  WHY: Phase 3 callers who rely on the docstring will mis-predict fingerprints. Reviewers rated this NIT.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1640-1641 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The `classify_validation_owner` docstring lists seven result fields, but the result dict also carries `truncated` (line 1663).
  WHY: Callers who rely on the docstring miss the signal that the classification was made over a capped list. Reviewers rated this NIT.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:6002 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_cmd_classify_validation_owner` runs the managed-path lookup, and `classify_validation_owner` requires `consumer_root` to be a directory (lines 1688-1689), even for a `harness_error` diagnosis whose owner is always `harness`.
  WHY: A lookup failure or a bad `--consumer-root` makes the CLI exit 2 with empty stdout, so the deterministic verdict is lost. Reviewers rated this NIT.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1533 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `_read_bounded_text` returns `""` on `OSError`, so an unreadable signature file becomes the default `no-error-lines` signature.
  WHY: Unrelated failures can share a fingerprint and dedup together. Gemini gave no severity; Sonnet rated this NIT.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:172-197 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `_VALIDATION_HEX_RUN_RE` leaves short SHA abbreviations made only of a-f characters (such as `abcdefa`) unmasked.
  WHY: Unstable fingerprints can treat the same harness failure as distinct incidents. Luna rated this NIT and Gemini gave no severity. Sonnet reviewed and dropped the same point as deliberate, so that reviewer disagrees.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1705-1732 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When the `fix_issues` or file lists are truncated, `classify_validation_owner` can return `project` or `none` without accounting for omitted harness-owned entries, instead of `mixed`.
  WHY: The harness part of a mixed failure is dropped and only `truncated: true` hints at it. Luna rated this NIT. Minimax mentioned it inside a docstring finding and said it was not asking for a change. Sonnet reviewed and dropped it as the safe direction.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
(No task gaps reported.)
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:6002 (`_cmd_classify_validation_owner`; matching `consumer_root` check in `classify_validation_owner`) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The CLI loads the managed-path list, and the classifier requires `consumer_root` to be a directory, whenever the diagnosis names any path, even for a `harness_error` diagnosis whose owner is always `harness`.
  WHY: If the lookup fails or `--consumer-root` is missing, the CLI exits 2 with empty stdout and the `harness` verdict is lost.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py (`_read_bounded_text`, used for `--signature-file`) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: An unreadable signature file becomes an empty signature, which normalizes to `no-error-lines`.
  WHY: Unrelated failures can share a fingerprint and dedup together. This stays low risk until a caller uses the CLI.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1563 and 1641 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `normalize_validation_signature` docstring is stale on hex masking, and the `classify_validation_owner` docstring omits the `truncated` field.
  WHY: This causes no runtime failure, but Phase 3 callers could mis-predict fingerprints and miss `truncated`.
- Task completeness: NONE. Reviewed and dropped: provenance gate for `validation_failure`, the a-f-only short hex regex, and truncated project lists that should be `mixed`.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: run the managed-path lookup and the `consumer_root` check only when `diagnosis.get("status") == "needs_fixes"` (about 3 lines).
- HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:172 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_VALIDATION_HEX_RUN_RE` fails to mask short SHA abbreviations made only of a-f characters, such as `abcdefa`.
  WHY: Unmasked short SHAs make fingerprints unstable, so identical harness failures are treated as distinct incidents.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1705-1710 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When `fix_issues` is truncated and all retained entries are harness-owned, the classifier returns `owner="none"` instead of accounting for potential project-owned issues among the truncated entries.
  WHY: Project-owned failures may be classified as `none` and not reported for human action.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1533 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `_read_bounded_text` silently returns an empty string on `OSError`, which `classify_validation_owner` turns into the default `no-error-lines` fingerprint.
  WHY: This masks signature-file read failures and groups different failures together, or splits the same one.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1560-1566 vs 195-197 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `normalize_validation_signature` docstring still says every hex run of 7-64 characters becomes `<sha>`, but the regex was narrowed. The docstring also does not mention the bare-name masking at lines 1550-1553.
  WHY: Phase 3 callers could mis-predict fingerprints and open a second heal lineage for the same failure. The doc/code mismatch is the defect.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1640-1641 vs 1663 (and 1730-1731) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `Returns` line omits `truncated`. A truncated fix-issue list whose retained entries are all project-owned returns `project`, not `mixed`.
  WHY: Callers never see `truncated`, and a mixed failure is filed as a pure project fix. The reviewer does not ask to change the project-vs-mixed design.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1688-1689 and 6002-6010 (verdict at 1696-1700) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Both new gates (managed-path lookup and the `consumer_root` ValueError) fire for a `harness_error` diagnosis, whose verdict is fixed as `harness` / `diagnosis_harness`.
  WHY: The CLI exits 2 with empty stdout when the support root is not a usable git checkout, the helper is not staged, or `--consumer-root` is bad. Guarding on `status == "needs_fixes"` fixes it.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS (1): scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py `_normalize_validation_signature_once`, lines 1550-1553. The bare repo name is masked with no length floor. Suggested fix: `if bare_name and len(bare_name) >= 6:` (1 line).
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS (2): scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py `load_validation_managed_paths`, line 1455. The child environment keeps credentials such as `GH_PAT` and `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Suggested fix: also drop names containing `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `_PAT`, `_API_KEY` (2 lines).
- HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:197 (`_VALIDATION_HEX_RUN_RE`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The regex leaves 7-39 character hex strings containing only a-f, such as `abcdefa`, unchanged.
  WHY: `validation_failure_fingerprint()` includes the unmasked signature, so the same harness failure can fingerprint differently when its abbreviated SHA changes.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1713-1732 (`classify_validation_owner()`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Truncated file lists or fix issues can be classified entirely as project-owned even when omitted paths or issues are harness-owned.
  WHY: The harness portion is dropped and the mixed ownership is not reported.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: NONE
- HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
